title: Quantifying LLM Biases Across Instruction Boundary in Mixed Question Forms

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the output distribution (Output Rate) and accuracy difference between frequently seen 'Dense' labels (e.g., True/False, Single Option) and infrequent 'Sparse' labels (e.g., Unknown, None Correct, Multiple Options) across mixed question forms.

Systematically modifying user prompts across an 'Instruction Boundary' framework (Sufficient, Redundant, and Insufficient settings) to evaluate how prompt variations (like vagueness, missing options, or prompt-polishing) induce reasoning errors and output shifts.
Testing how models adapt their answers when user instructions explicitly suggest a specific label (dense or sparse) or when exposed to redundant, misleading information and skewed few-shot examples.
